source: Dhami et al. (2024) Effects of task structure and confirmation bias in alternative hypotheses evaluation
finding: Human anchor for this angle. Study 1 put the same hypothesis-evidence task in three layouts. Hypotheses in rows and evidence in columns cut reliance on confirming-only evidence. The ACH-style layout (hypotheses in columns) did not.
numbers: N=161, random assignment: HypCol n=55, HypRow n=51, HypText n=55. Task 1 chose Hypothesis-B (balanced or inconsistent strategy): HypCol 38.2%, HypRow 60.8%, HypText 32.7%. chi2(2)=9.43, p=.009, effect .24. HypRow post hoc p=.003; HypCol p=.327.
limits: One task decides strategy (Task 1), two hypotheses, lab students on paper. Authors say replication with varied numbers of hypotheses and evidence is needed. No machine data.
agent_relevance: Layout changes which strategy a reader uses. No LLM study has re-run this three-layout design. It is a cheap open test for our agent.

source: Dhami et al. (2024) Effects of task structure and confirmation bias in alternative hypotheses evaluation
finding: Layout did not change sensitivity to evidence credibility. Study 2 found trained Dutch analysts mostly did not show confirmation bias with the ACH layout.
numbers: Study 1 credibility switch (A in Task 3A to B in 3B): HypCol 77%, HypRow 78%, HypText 75%; chi2(2)=0.15, p=.927. Study 2 N=62 analysts: balanced-strategy users 98% sensitive to credibility vs consistent-only 72.7% vs inconsistent-only 33.3%. Task 1 consistent-only users had CRT M=0.27 vs M=0.81 for the others (Glass d=0.54).
limits: CRT range tiny (mean 0.51 of 3). Authors explain the row effect by horizontal reading and sequential per-hypothesis processing; this was not tested.
agent_relevance: A matrix per se does not help. Layout moves strategy, not weighting. Measure strategy choice, not only accuracy.

source: He et al. (2024) Does Prompt Formatting Have Any Impact on LLM Performance?
finding: Same content in plain text, Markdown, JSON and YAML moved GPT scores a lot. GPT-3.5 was fragile; GPT-4 was steadier. No format won across models.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo accuracy on an MMLU international-law set rose 42% for JSON vs Markdown. Code translation varied up to 40%. FIND: about 200% gain for plain text over Markdown on GPT-3.5. HumanEval: GPT-4-32k gained over 300% going from JSON to plain text. MMLU consistency (same answer across formats): GPT-3.5 below 0.5, only 16% identical for Markdown vs JSON; GPT-4 above 0.5.
limits: GPT family only. No HTML or XML. One-sided matched-pair t-tests on best vs worst template (p mostly below .01). Percent changes may sit on small bases.
agent_relevance: Presentation format is a first-order variable for the S4 step. Pick it per model with a small test. Larger models are less sensitive.

source: He et al. (2024) Does Prompt Formatting Have Any Impact on LLM Performance? (transfer)
finding: Best format flips by model: GPT-3.5-turbo preferred JSON, GPT-4 preferred Markdown. Formats do not transfer between model series.
numbers: Overlap (IoU) of top templates between model series often below 0.2; within one sub-series (e.g. gpt-35-turbo vs 16k) above 0.7.
limits: Template set chosen by the authors; per-benchmark sample sizes not recorded in this read.
agent_relevance: If the base model changes, re-test the presentation code. Keep the S4 format a configurable field.

source: Sui et al. (2024) Table Meets LLM: Can LLMs Understand Structured Table Data? (WSDM 2024)
finding: SUC benchmark of seven table-structure tasks. Markup matters. HTML was best on average; Markdown was poor on column retrieval.
numbers: GPT-3.5 downstream: TabFact HTML 71.33% vs NL+Sep 70.26% vs Markdown 68.40%. HybridQA HTML 47.29 vs NL+Sep 45.02. Size detection (count rows and columns): HTML 67.00%, NL+Sep 42.00%, Markdown 40.67%. Column retrieval: HTML 63.33%, NL+Sep 60.67%, Markdown 35.33%. Row retrieval: HTML 42.00, Markdown 42.33, NL+Sep 31.00. Cell lookup only 39.67-44.00%. GPT-4 on 300-sample subsets scored higher everywhere (size detection 83.43% HTML).
limits: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 only. Authors guess HTML helps because of code and web training data (untested). They report HTML over NL+Sep as a 6.76% improvement.
agent_relevance: A table reaches the model through its serialization. Counting rows and columns is weak. Use explicit tags or ids, and let code do counts.

source: Sui et al. (2024) Table Meets LLM (self-augmented prompting)
finding: Having the model first write out table structure knowledge (key values, ranges), then answer, gave small gains on table tasks.
numbers: Gains over the best input design: TabFact 2.31%, HybridQA 2.13%, SQA 2.72%, Feverous 0.84%, ToTTo 5.68%.
limits: Small gains. Needs two model calls. GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: A cheap two-step S4: restate structure, then reason. Gain is small and will not fix a bad layout.

source: Liu, Wang, Chen (2023) Rethinking Tabular Data Understanding with Large Language Models
finding: Transposing a table or shuffling its rows hurts LLMs. Text reasoning lost 12 to 37 percent; a code-running agent lost far more when transposed.
numbers: GPT-3.5 accuracy, original / shuffle / transpose / transpose+shuffle. Direct prompting: 59.50 / 52.21 (-12.25%) / 51.14 (-14.05%) / 37.51 (-36.96%). Python-shell agent: 55.91 / 47.91 (-14.31%) / 12.45 (-77.73%) / 8.96 (-83.97%).
limits: Row order of the four table values is inferred from the percent drops in a garbled extract. GPT-3.5 only. Authors say column shuffling had minimal effect.
agent_relevance: Orientation (headers in first row vs first column) is not neutral for models. Normalize to one canonical layout before reasoning, and test both orientations.

source: Deng et al. (2024) Tables as Texts or Images: Evaluating Table Reasoning of LLMs and MLLMs
finding: Compared five text and three image table forms. Text vs image depends on model and data. GPT-4 used clues better from the image on a long numeric table; on Wikipedia tables text won.
numbers: Row coloring in the image: GPT-4 51.8% vs 56.2% without color; Gemini Pro 39.4% vs 36.8%. For GPT-4 expert prompting beat vanilla by 3.5% and CoT by 1.2%; for GPT-3.5 with linearized tables CoT beat vanilla by 2.7% and expert by 4.2%. Llama-2 vs GPT-4 gap up to 15% on FinQA and 22.9% on TabFact.
limits: Some figures read from a garbled extract; dataset behind each number not fully checked. Visual results are model-specific.
agent_relevance: Visual layout does not help models the way it helps people. Test per model. Coloring can hurt.

source: Tam et al. (2024) Let Me Speak Freely? Impact of Format Restrictions on LLM Performance
finding: Forcing JSON, XML or YAML output lowered reasoning accuracy; stricter format meant bigger drop. Classification tasks gained from constraint.
numbers: Of GPT-3.5 JSON-mode responses on Last Letter, 100% put the answer key before the reason key, which gave direct answering instead of chain of thought. Reasoning tasks (GSM8K, Last Letter, Shuffled Objects) fell; classification (e.g. MultiFin) gained. One setting showed a 38.15% gap between formats.
limits: Per-model deltas not extracted from figure text. Models: GPT-3.5, Claude-3-haiku, Gemini-1.5-flash, LLaMA-3-8B, Gemma-2-9B. Only one-reason-one-answer schemas.
agent_relevance: In any output schema keep the reasoning field before the answer field. Use rigid structure for classification outputs, relaxed text for reasoning.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying LMs' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (ICLR 2024)
finding: Meaning-preserving formatting changes (separators, casing, spacing) moved few-shot accuracy a lot, even with bigger models or more examples.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B between equivalent formats; about 10 points average over 50+ tasks. GPT-3.5: up to 56 points, median spread 6.4 points, across 320 formats. Median task spread 7.5 points; several tasks over 70.
limits: Mostly open models, few-shot. Format rankings correlate weakly across models.
agent_relevance: Report results over several layouts. A one-layout result for our agent is weak evidence.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with LLMs
finding: Order of premises changes accuracy. Best when order matches the proof order. Order is a presentation variable like row order in a matrix.
numbers: Permuting premise order dropped deductive accuracy by over 30%. On R-GSM, GPT-4-turbo and PaLM 2-L fell by up to 20-30% relative to GSM8K.
limits: Logic and math, not evidence weighing.
agent_relevance: Order evidence by the reasoning path (group by hypothesis) when building the S4 view. Shuffled order has a hidden cost.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Position in the prompt matters: accuracy is highest for information at the start or end and lowest in the middle (U shape).
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo closed-book 56.1%, oracle 88.3%; with 20 documents, answers in the middle fall below the closed-book level.
limits: QA and key-value retrieval. Seen in long-context models too.
agent_relevance: In a long evidence matrix put critical cells and the question at the edges.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) LLMs Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors (ICLR 2024)
finding: Models prefer certain option IDs (A, B, C, D). Moving the right answer to another slot changes accuracy sharply. PriDe debiasing helps.
numbers: On 1,000 MMLU items with 250 answers per slot, llama-30B chose A/B/C/D 34.6/27.3/22.3/15.8% of the time. Moving gold to A raised vicuna-33B from 57.0% to 68.2%; to D gave 41.2%.
limits: Authors say bias is mainly token bias on option IDs, not slot position.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis labels (H1, H2) may act like option IDs. Rotate labels across runs to avoid a bias that looks like confirmation bias.

source: Li et al. (2023) Table-GPT: Table-tuned GPT for Diverse Table Tasks
finding: Vanilla GPT-3.5 often fails basic table-structure tests. Table tuning fixes it. Tables are nearly invariant to row or column permutation for people but not for models.
numbers: Missing-cell finding on 1,000 sampled real tables: GPT-3.5 failed up to 74% of tests, naming wrong column or row id.
limits: Fixes need fine-tuning, outside a scaffold-only plan.
agent_relevance: Matrix reading is a weak spot. Offload cell location to code.

source: Lee, Kang, Shin (2026) Make LLMs See Like Investigators: Structured Analysis in Investigative Reasoning (ACL 2026)
finding: Four-agent scaffold (PRISM) filters evidence, profiles each suspect, builds an evidence-by-suspect consistency matrix (ACH), then judges. It beat direct, CoT, persona and self-consistency on MuSR murder mysteries across 10 LLMs.
numbers: Average accuracy: Direct 58.1%, CoT 57.2%, Persona 58.2%, P-CoT 58.0%, Self-Consistency (5 samples) 63.2%, PRISM 71.3% (+13.2 points; +6.0 Ministral-8B to +22.0 GPT-5.2). GPT-5.2: 58.0% to 80.0%. CoT hurt Llama-3.1-8B, Mixtral-8x7B (-4.8) and Qwen3-14B (-2.0).
limits: MuSR only; four agents cost more tokens than one call. Matrix orientation is not varied.
agent_relevance: Structure that tells the model what to compare beats generic reasoning prompts. See next line: the matrix itself is the small part.

source: Lee, Kang, Shin (2026) PRISM ablation
finding: Information filtering alone gave 63.8%. Adding the M.O.M.A. suspect profile added 6.7 points. Adding the ACH matrix on top added only 0.8 points.
numbers: Filter+judge 63.8%; plus M.O.M.A 70.5%; full 71.3%. Combined structure gain +7.5 points: M.O.M.A 89%, ACH 11%.
limits: Average over 10 models; one-culprit narratives; the ACH matrix is built from the profiles, so its gain depends on the earlier step.
agent_relevance: Per-hypothesis (per-suspect) profiling mattered more than the matrix. This echoes the hypotheses-in-rows, one-block-per-hypothesis result in Dhami et al. (analogy, not tested).

source: Roberts (2025) LLM SATs FTW (via sats4llms wiki page on ACH)
finding: Practitioner ACH tool: generate hypotheses, then evidence for and against each in separate calls, then score each pair. Single-prompt ACH is called a failure mode.
numbers: Scale -5 to +5 per pair. Query count = 1 + N hypotheses + N + M pairs. Built with GPT-4, LangChain, Pydantic.
limits: Blog and wiki claims. No accuracy or bias numbers. The priming explanation is the wiki's reading.
agent_relevance: Cell-by-cell calls are presentation by code: the model never sees the whole matrix. Worth testing against whole-matrix prompts.

source: suprathermal (2024) ACH-Grounding (via sats4llms wiki)
finding: The LLM only fills matrix cells with local one-pair judgments. Deterministic code ranks hypotheses and computes likelihoods. Earlier outputs are fed back as context.
numbers: Token cost O((|E|+|H|)^2). Approval asked above $1 estimated cost. No accuracy numbers.
limits: Author says not production-ready. No validation.
agent_relevance: Concrete S4 pattern: build the matrix in code, ask the model per cell, total in code. Cost grows fast.

source: Yousuf et al. (2024) LLM Augmentations to Support Analytical Reasoning over Multiple Documents
finding: Intelligence-analysis agent builds an evidence graph over a dossier and retrieves from it. It beat plain-LLM baselines on relevance classification and narrative quality.
numbers: Classification F1 on three datasets: clustering baseline 0.65 / 0.72 / 0.56; full augmentation 0.81 / 0.78 / 0.65. Narrative quality on a 1-7 scale.
limits: Small public datasets (Crescent, Manpad, Atlantic Storm). Paper warns ROUGE and METEOR misjudge intelligence narratives.
agent_relevance: A graph is another presentation form. Rows-vs-columns vs graph was not compared.

source: Zhong et al. (2026) Before the Action: Benchmarking LLMs on Prospective Hypothesis Discovery (HypoArena)
finding: Benchmark for building a hypothesis space from inconclusive evidence. Pairwise judging agrees with expert judgment.
numbers: 988 cases in six domains (HypoData); 15 frontier LLMs; Bradley-Terry-Davidson ranking plus a six-dimension rubric.
limits: Only abstract and introduction read. No layout condition.
agent_relevance: Possible source of items for open hypothesis generation, which precedes any matrix.

source: sats4llms wiki: ACH page (layout note)
finding: The wiki page does not describe a matrix orientation for LLM versions; it says only that the manual method has hypotheses across the top and evidence down the side.
numbers: Zero studies found that vary hypotheses-in-rows vs hypotheses-in-columns for an LLM.
limits: Absence of evidence. Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate-limited and the arXiv API returned nothing, and the web search budget ran out after two searches, so coverage is partial.
agent_relevance: Cheap experiment: HypRow vs HypCol vs text on Dhami Tasks 1, 3A and 3B; measure consistent-only strategy and credibility switching.

source: Synthesis across Sui, Liu, Deng, He on table layout
finding: Derived by this agent. The same table gives different results by markup, orientation, row order and even color. Effects run from a few points to tens of points; the best form differs by model.
numbers: HTML beats NL+Sep by up to 25 points on size detection (Sui); transpose -12% and transpose+shuffle -37% on direct prompting (Liu).
limits: Different tasks and models; numbers are not additive.
agent_relevance: Use a labelled-cell or HTML-like format, one fixed orientation, and re-test per model.

source: Synthesis across Tam, Sclar, He on format sensitivity
finding: Derived by this agent. Input layout and output schema both matter. An answer-before-reasoning schema removed chain of thought entirely in GPT-3.5 JSON-mode.
numbers: Tam: 100% answer-first in GPT-3.5 JSON-mode; Sclar: up to 76 points between equivalent formats.
limits: Different tasks.
agent_relevance: Lint the output schema in code so reasoning fields come first.

source: Dhami et al. (2024) judgmental coherence and cognitive-load discussion
finding: Authors argue the ACH layout forces simultaneous processing of all hypotheses per evidence item, while hypotheses-in-rows allows sequential per-hypothesis reading. Both are untested mechanisms. Coherence did not depend on layout.
numbers: Deviation from additivity overall M=17.59 (SD 13.59); layout effect F(2,160)=1.22, p=.299. Superadditive/additive/subadditive: HypCol 41.8/1.8/56.4%, HypRow 39.2/3.9/56.9%, HypText 41.8/7.3/50.9%.
limits: Mechanism proposed, not measured.
agent_relevance: For an LLM the cost is attention over a long linear string. Hypotheses-in-rows gives one contiguous block per hypothesis, like the PRISM profile step.

source: Lee, Kang, Shin (2026) PRISM: self-consistency vs structure
finding: Five-sample self-consistency (63.2%) helped less than structured analysis (71.3%) and information filtering alone (63.8%) matched it. The authors say the bottleneck is quality of attention, not quantity of reasoning.
numbers: SC 63.2% vs Direct 58.1% (+5.1); PRISM beats SC by 8.1 points. GPT-5.2 was 5th of 10 at Direct (58.0%); Ministral-8B led Direct at 62.8%.
limits: Single benchmark (MuSR), accuracy averaged over 10 models.
agent_relevance: Spend tokens on choosing and arranging evidence before spending them on more samples.
